caption: A car driving along an icy street brakes hard, its wheels lock, and it slides on past the stop line before it comes to a halt.

sa.check: A car drives along an icy street.
It slides on past the stop line and comes to a halt beyond it.
The stop line painted on the road is visible.
The braking comes first, then the locked wheels, then the slide.

pc.expect: Once the wheels lock the car keeps going the way it was travelling and slows gradually, coming to rest past the line.
pc.fail: The car stops on the spot as soon as the wheels lock; or it keeps sliding at its old speed and never comes to rest; or it slides backward.

pc.expect: The car slides along its own line on the ice; nothing turns it or sets it going again.
pc.fail: The car swerves sharply on the open, straight road with nothing striking it; or it moves off again after coming to rest; or it gathers speed while the wheels are locked.

pc.expect: The wheels are visibly still while the body slides on over the ice.
pc.fail: The wheels keep rolling with the road while the car is plainly skidding; or the wheels turn backward while the car slides forward; or the wheels lock and the car halts in the same instant.

pc.expect: Loose snow and ice chips thrown up at the tyres fall back to the road.
pc.fail: Spray hangs in the air after the car has stopped; or it is flung forward ahead of the car; or ice chips rise away from the road and keep rising.
pc.precondition: Loose snow, slush or spray is visibly disturbed at the tyres.

pc.expect: One car keeps its shape on the road and stays outside every other solid thing.
pc.fail: The car vanishes or a second one appears; or it passes through another vehicle or a kerb; or it changes into a different car mid-slide.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The car's colour, the road markings and the street stay the same.
pc.fail: The car changes colour; or the stop line moves along the road between frames; or the buildings alongside rearrange.
